answer: Graduated Non-Transferable Ledger Depth. Each identity must hold an onyx-tier ledger balance funded only by inbound payments, and its spend ceiling scales sublinearly with ledger age—fresh clones clear tiny amounts. Because value must traverse a walnut-shaped transfer graph before it can be spent, an attacker pays full transfer friction per clone but recovers almost nothing. Cost is linear per identity while yield stays near zero, so mass cloning destroys capital faster than it earns. A canyon of dead balances, not a gate.
